comment: The glossary of record as data. docs/reference/vocabulary.md is the page people read; this file is what the tools read: scripts/vocabulary-fix (the check and the fixer) and `make vocabulary`. Edit this file, then run `scripts/vocabulary-fix --docs` to rewrite the page's tables. Not legal advice: the safety notes live in the private research file.

rules.people-read: What a person reads (screens, documentation, command help and output, the `error` and `next` sentences, MCP descriptions, notices, chart comments) uses the product words. Screens and messages the server builds ask the terms system ({key}, terms().label) so a rename takes effect; documentation names the default word and, once per page that introduces a level, the plain word beside it. Never a hard-coded plain level name where the level is meant.
rules.identifiers: Stable identifiers (API JSON fields and paths, database tables and columns, configuration keys and kind names, command-line flags, metric names, event kinds, Go identifiers) cannot follow a renameable word. Each level has one neutral, permanent name: installation, organization, unit, project. They are documented as 'the API name of a Base' and are never themed.
rules.ordinary-words: Where an industry word is the accepted term it stays ordinary: pipeline, step, run, branch, commit, pull request, secret, environment, deploy, rollback, variable, template, library, runner, artifact, registry.
rules.buttons: Ordinary verb on the button, product noun for the thing: the button says Approve or Reject; the thing a person gives is a clearance; the recorded answer is Go or No-go. Pull-request reviews keep the ordinary word approval; the pipeline key stays kind: approval.
rules.capitals: Level and feature words are common nouns: lower case in the middle of a sentence (the base, a wing, a flight plan), capitalized at the start of a sentence, in a heading, a label or a button. Wingman and Launchway are names: always capitalized.
rules.spelling: American English: organization, color, behavior, license (noun and verb), initialize, customize.
rules.disclaimer: These are ordinary words used descriptively. Launchway is not affiliated with or endorsed by any military service.

terms.meaning: The whole installation, and every customer's own walled-off space on the hosted service: the top level.
terms.appears: navigation, first-run wizard, settings, sign-up, hosted-service docs

terms.meaning: The group that owns the projects: the second level.
An optional group of projects with shared settings: the third level.
mustNotBeCalled: team (when the default words are in effect)

terms.meaning: One repository and its pipeline: the fourth level.
mustNotBeCalled: app (that is an application, a deployed thing)

terms.meaning: The helper panel beside every page: where you are and what you can do next.
terms.appears: the panel, the first-run wizard, learn pages

terms.meaning: The checks made before a run, a merge or a deploy.
terms.appears: run and deploy pages, policy docs

terms.meaning: The list of things that must be true before a change goes on.
A person decides whether a change may go on, by saying Go or No-go.
terms.appears: run pages, the decisions list, settings, policies
mustNotBeCalled: gate (for the thing a person gives)

terms.meaning: The recorded answer that lets the run continue. The button says Approve in both sets.
The recorded answer that fails the step. The button says Reject in both sets.
A time when changes may not go out.
mustNotBeCalled: code freeze (use freeze in the plain set)

terms.meaning: A complete, ready-made pipeline for a kind of project, with a few things to fill in.
terms.appears: new project, template library, learn pages
mustNotBeCalled: pipeline template (a step template is a different thing)

terms.meaning: The append-only record of who did what, and when.
A change on its way to production.
The path a change travels, from commit to production. Named after the product, so the same in both sets.
mustNotBeCalled: pipeline view (a pipeline is the definition; the launch line is the path of one change)

terms.meaning: The agent on the customer's side that does the work and holds the data, so the hosted service holds nothing sensitive.
terms.appears: hosted-service roadmap; not yet in the product

today.layer: variables API, CLI flags, MCP schemas
today.name: installation, organization, unit, project
today.note: American; organisation accepted as an alias

stableNames.recommendation: Keep installation, organization, unit, project as the permanent API names. Make organization (American) canonical in the configuration kind, the overview JSON and the Go types with organisation accepted as a documented read alias for at least two releases. Do not number the levels and do not use the aviation words as identifiers.

checks.use: the American spelling (organization, color, behavior, license, initialize, customize ...)
the level word through the terms system ({organization}), or write the plain word
the top level word ({installation}: Base) or 'customer'
the Logbook ({logbook}) or, in plain description, the audit trail
the guide ({guide}: Wingman); 'assistant' stays only for a third-party AI assistant that connects through MCP
the terms system when the level is meant ({organization}, {installation}); ordinary use (an organization's identity provider; installing software) may stay and goes on the allow list
lower case in the middle of a sentence
clearance for the thing a person gives; approval stays for pull-request reviews and the step key
flight plan (a whole ready-made pipeline) or step template (a reusable part)
